rounds.text: Homre Ltd is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a massive 1766% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E14] and a 30% compounded profit growth in the same period [E18]. The company is demonstrating superior capital efficiency compared to its peers, with an ROCE of 37.65% against a sector benchmark of 10.27% [E10]. This efficiency is further validated by an ROA of 6.52%, which also outpaces the sector benchmark of 4.96% [E8]. Crucially, the business is generating real cash, producing Rs 0.70 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 0.33 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E32, E33]. While the market remains focused on historical metrics, the company is actively improving its profitability, as seen in the quarterly operating margin rising to 4% in September 2026 from -1% in the year-ago quarter [E28]. Conceded: the company faces significant valuation headwinds with a P/E of 190x [E6], a negative ROE of -8.22% [E9], and a high debt-to-equity ratio of 1.84x [E34].

Homre Ltd trades at a highly demanding valuation that is disconnected from its underlying fundamental reality, featuring a trailing P/E of 47.3x and a price-to-book multiple of 23.38x [E1, E2], with independent key ratios suggesting an even more extreme P/E of 190x and P/B of 131.81x against sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. This pricing leaves zero margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at Rs 1 per share against a market price of Rs 1.87, resulting in a -55.8% margin of safety and a reverse DCF that demands an unrealistic 20.1% earnings growth rate [E42, E43, E44]. Furthermore, the balance sheet carries severe structural vulnerabilities, including a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.84x where total debt exceeds net worth and a critical current ratio of 0.51x indicating that current liabilities vastly exceed current assets [E34, E35]. Profitability metrics are deeply troubled, evidenced by a negative ROE of -8.22% and a median 3-year ROE of -38%, accompanied by warnings that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E9, E25, E51]. Promoter confidence is also eroding as insider ownership dropped by 3.59 percentage points from December 2023 to September 2026, alongside a -0.96% decline in the latest quarter [E38, E49]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reached an impressive 1766% and ROCE stands at a strong 37.65% [E10, E14].

The bear’s focus on valuation multiples like P/E and P/B [E1, E2, E6, E7] ignores the company’s explosive growth trajectory, where sales have surged 1766% in the trailing twelve months [E14]. While the bear cites a DCF model [E42, E43], this static valuation fails to account for the company’s recent operational turnaround, where net profit grew 325% year-over-year [E55] and quarterly operating margins expanded by 4 percentage points [E28]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio is 1.84x and the current ratio is 0.51x [E34, E35]. However, the bear overlooks that the company is already generating positive free cash flow of Rs 0.33 Cr [E33] and has successfully begun reducing its total borrowings [E36]. Furthermore, the criticism of ROE [E9, E25] ignores the company’s superior capital efficiency, evidenced by a robust ROCE of 37.65%, which significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.27% [E10]. Finally, while the bear highlights a decline in promoter holdings [E38, E49], it fails to acknowledge that the company is currently outperforming expectations, with profit growth now exceeding price growth [E46].

The bull’s dismissal of valuation concerns relies on a trailing twelve-month sales spike of 1766% [E14], but fails to address that the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 47.3x [E1] and an egregious P/B of 23.38x [E2], with data providers flagging the P/E as high as 190x against sector benchmarks [E6]. Conceded: net profit grew 325% year-over-year [E55]. However, the bull's reliance on this recent growth glosses over a severe DCF overvaluation of -55.8% [E43], a reverse DCF requirement of 20.1% growth that exceeds base expectations [E44], and a multi-year negative median ROE reaching -38% over three years [E25]. While the bull points to positive free cash flow of Rs 0.33 Cr [E33], it glosses over the alarming current ratio of 0.51x indicating that current liabilities severely exceed current assets [E35]. Furthermore, the bull’s defense of capital structure ignores a precarious debt-to-equity ratio of 1.84x where total debt exceeds net worth [E34], alongside negative long-term ROE readings of -8.22% against the sector [E9]. Finally, the bull downplays promoter selling by citing recent outperformance, but ignores that promoter holdings have dropped by 3.59 percentage points over time [E38] and specifically fell last quarter [E49].
